name: Iranian nationalism
summary: Iranian nationalism centres on pride in Iran's ancient history, Persian language and culture, and national unity and sovereignty. As a state ideology it was secular, modernizing and centralizing under the Pahlavis, and it also took an anti-colonial, sovereignty-first form in Mossadegh's National Front. It stresses territorial integrity, resists foreign interference, and tends to treat Persian identity as the core of the nation.
scope: The mainstream secular nationalism of the late Qajar reformers (Akhundzadeh, Kermani), the Pahlavi state ideology of Reza Shah and his son, and Mossadegh's oil-nationalization nationalism, with the Pan-Iranist current as a related strand. It excludes the post-1979 Islamic Republic's Shia-religious national identity and minority-ethnic nationalisms such as Azeri or Kurdish. Adherents split on monarchy versus parliamentary democracy, so those answers are low confidence.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nationalism as a movement had no wage program; adherents range from Pahlavi modernizers to National Front reformers.

public-ownership.rationale: Oil nationalization under Mossadegh is the movement's signature economic act, and Reza Shah's state industrialization favoured state control of strategic sectors.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nationalists did not make wealth taxation a defining issue; adherents are split between landed-elite monarchists and reformers.

unions-good.rationale: Labor organizing was not a nationalist theme, and Reza Shah's state suppressed independent organizing.

property-fundamental.rationale: Reza Shah seized clerical endowments yet protected landed and urban property; no settled doctrine.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nationalism is not syndicalist; ownership by the nation and state, not workers, is the idea.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Reza Shah and his successor relied on secret police and security-first rule, which the movement's state form accepted.

strong-leader.rationale: Reza Shah governed as a one-man leader and is credited by defenders with unifying the country, a model Pahlavi nationalists praised.

state-harmful.rationale: Nationalism builds and glorifies the centralized state; Reza Shah's program was state construction.

empower-police-military.rationale: Reza Shah's modern army and police were instruments of national unity, with military spending rising fivefold.

decide-locally.rationale: Centralization against tribes and provinces was a defining nationalist policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Pahlavi modernizers pushed women's unveiling and mixed-sex venues, while nationalists valued cultural continuity; split.

more-religion-public.rationale: Most nationalists are secular and stress the pre-Islamic past; Reza Shah curbed clerical influence.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Pride in history, culture and language is the core of Iranian nationalism.

gradual-change.rationale: Reza Shah imposed rapid top-down change, such as dress, law and language reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a central topic for Iran; adherents have no settled position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Mossadegh insisted the UN Security Council had no jurisdiction over Iranian oil, which stressed sovereignty over international bodies.

nation-first.rationale: Mossadegh's independence politics put national interest above foreign claims, though not hostility to cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Strong defense of non-interference in internal affairs, shaped by experience of foreign intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Territorial integrity and national identity are central; open borders are alien to the ideology.

limit-growth.rationale: Nationalist modernizers prized industrialization and growth.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Modernization through technology and infrastructure was a Pahlavi-era goal.

revolution-justified.rationale: Pahlavi nationalists were order-oriented; the Mossadegh strand took legal channels, though the Constitutional Revolution is honoured.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Pahlavi state built domestic industry and curtailed foreign economic privileges.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State institutions drove industrialization, with industrial plants up 17-fold under Reza Shah.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nationalism is compatible with market economy and state; no tradition of abolishing wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The state took over money printing through the National Bank, a nationalist achievement.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Authoritarian state coordination existed but not a stated doctrine.

one-party-rule.rationale: Reza Shah ruled personally; the Mossadegh strand was parliamentary; a single party is not the ideology's form.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Pahlavi state ideology was monarchist and diaspora nationalists often are, but the Mossadegh strand was constitutional and adherents split.

democracy-best.rationale: Mossadegh appealed to the national will, while Pahlavi nationalism was authoritarian; adherents split.

workers-councils.rationale: Alien to a nationalist, state-centered ideology.

right-to-secede.rationale: Territorial integrity is a central concern, with losses in the Caucasus remembered as a grievance.

natural-rulers.rationale: Aryan-origin and dynastic claims exist but no explicit doctrine.

political-violence-never.rationale: Reza Shah crushed rivals and tribes by force; adherents do not hold pacifism.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not a stated doctrine, though military is valued.

separate-church-state.rationale: Reza Shah curbed clergy, closed religious schools and secularized courts; most nationalists are secular.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Replacement of Islamic courts with European-style law was a nationalist policy, though a religious-nationalist minority exists.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement centered a monopoly of state force against tribal and local rivals.

military-superiority.rationale: National army-building and prestige were a priority, with military spending soaring.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism defined Iranian identity via Persians and Aryan origin; multi-ethnic strands exist, so only moderately.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nationalism sees the nation, not class, as the unit of history.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism counters pan-Turkism and pan-Arabism with Iranian unity, rather than uniting with other Muslim states.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Fast modernization is characteristic, though disruption of institutions is a stretch.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revives a glorious past yet seeks modernity; split.

direct-action.rationale: The Mossadegh strand used parliament and legal means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the modernizing, industrializing program of Pahlavi-era nationalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A Marxist distribution principle that nationalists, who put the nation above class, do not hold.

production-for-use.rationale: A Marxist economic idea that nationalist platforms did not take up.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist concept; nationalists framed exploitation as foreign.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine that nationalism, which subordinates class to nation, rejects.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivization is alien to Iranian nationalist platforms, which did not propose it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist claim; nationalists blamed foreign powers specifically.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement built a strong taxing and spending state.

conscription.rationale: The Pahlavi state built a mass army, and conscription served national unification.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalist loyalty to homeland is opposite to exit.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Aryanism in Reza Shah's era used racial theories but not an explicit claim about racial ability genetics.

total-state.rationale: Pahlavi state directed culture and education but not as an ideology of total control; adherents mostly reject totalitarianism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pahlavi-era nationalism and Qajar reformers called for revival of Iran's lost glory.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Mainstream pan-Iranism lacks irredentist aims, while radical streams want expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Replaced tribal and local authority with a modern bureaucratic state.

bound-labor.rationale: Serf-style land bondage contradicts the modernizing program of Pahlavi-era nationalism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Persian language was promoted and purged of Arabic words by an academy, but Persian had not fallen out of use, so this is indirect.

school-vouchers.rationale: State-run secular education was central to Pahlavi nationalism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Mossadegh framed national independence as universal and every nation's right.

force-without-un.rationale: Strong sovereignty claims against UN authority, but no stated policy on force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Secular Qajar reformers like Akhundzadeh favored rational modernity and treated Islam as a later layer.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism subordinates class to nation, so cooperation is the norm.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Pride in Iran's history, monuments and culture is central to the ideology, so sacrificing heritage is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-foreign sentiment present, but no documented common-front doctrine in sources.

workers-nation.rationale: National identity is placed above class identity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reza Shah's unveiling campaign and admission of women to professions went against sex-distinct public roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Secular modernizing state built a national bank and modern finance.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a part of Iranian nationalism, which centers on shared nation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist concept; nationalism stresses the state as national.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Oil is the key national resource; the dispute was over who controls it, and nationalists favour using it for development.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Persianization and a unified national identity were official policy.

elite-replacement.rationale: Replacement conspiracy theories are not part of Iranian nationalism as documented.

national-mission.rationale: Nationalists claim independence, not exporting a government form.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

reviewHistory.rationale: Mossadegh named government corruption as a problem, along with foreign interference.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about one government, party or regime, or about fighting corruption, not a general claim that most politicians put their own interests first, which this statement now asks.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not part of the documented ideology, though Aryanist racial thinking existed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nationalist programs built an interventionist state, so a minimal state is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Aryanism existed, but no explicit doctrine against intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Mainstream nationalism accepts equal rights on paper, though Persian ethnocentrism is documented.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist strategic debate that nationalists did not engage in.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Reza Shah replaced religious courts with a uniform European-style legal system.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Reza Shah's secular education and closed private religious schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Mossadegh invoked the will of the Iranian nation as the source of legitimacy for nationalization.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced settlement of tribes happened, yet no doctrine of expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement's state-builders used force against tribes and rivals.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Mossadegh framed liberty against foreign domination, but this is about states, not persons.

separated-powers.rationale: Parliament was a decorative cover in Reza Shah's rule, while the constitutional tradition favored it.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist principle that nationalism rejects as foreign class politics.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism pursued homogenization and viewed linguistic diversity as a threat to unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is foreign to the movement, which favoured appointed bureaucracy and monarchy or parliament.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Reza Shah's regime was repressive in the name of unity and order.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Pahlavi state used control over media and culture, yet it was not party-based.

party-commands-army.rationale: The monarch or state commanded the army, not a party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sovereignty and non-interference are central to the Mossadegh strand.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Pahlavi monarchy held command of the military and chose ministers, though the Mossadegh strand disputed it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Shia Islam has no bishops, so the question does not apply to Iranian nationalism.

clerical-rule.rationale: The secular nationalists conflicted with clergy, and the 1979 shift to Shia identity marginalized them.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Foreign to nationalism, which calls for national unity.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Forced home ownership is not part of any documented nationalist program.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replaced tribal forces with a professional national army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Modernizers valued urban industrial modernity, with tribes sedentarized.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Iranism holds that Iranian peoples were separated by outside powers, though the mainstream version has no irredentist aims.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Aryanist and pride-in-civilization ideas assert Iran's distinctive greatness.

minority-language-support.rationale: Reza Shah banned minority languages; later leniency was limited, and critics demand support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Uniform law was pursued against clerical and religious jurisdictions, so special exemptions are disfavoured.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Reza Shah imposed uniform dress and conduct, which runs against encouraging nonconformity.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Mossadegh nationalized oil to eradicate foreign influence and improve economic conditions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Reza Shah's authoritarian modernization is defended on these grounds.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The head of state under Pahlavi was a hereditary monarch.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state took control of national currency issue.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial losses are a core grievance; a concession of land would be rejected.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Mossadegh justified nationalization on national interest.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Territory lost to Russia and elsewhere is viewed as unjustly separated.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Reza Shah seized endowments, curbed clergy, and secularized schooling and courts.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Pahlavi monarchy cast the Shah as national symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Reza Shah used force to subdue provincial and tribal rivals and centralize.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The movement aimed at a centralizing unitary state, not regional legal autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Aryamehr title was the Light of the Aryans, not divine descent.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Pahlavi rule was autocratic, yet the constitutional tradition rejects it.

leader-cult.rationale: Pahlavi propaganda glorified the Shah, with titles and imagery.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that nationalists reject.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Radical pan-Iranist streams claim lands inhabited by Iranian peoples, while mainstream does not.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Secular nationalists opposed religious penal law and curbed clerical power.

women-must-cover.rationale: Reza Shah banned the chador and mandated unveiling, so the opposite compulsion.

common-currency.rationale: State control over currency was a nationalist gain.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism seeks cultural ties and radical wings political union.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Official policy rejected minority institutions, imposing Persian.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nationalists see culture and the nation as the drivers.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Reza Shah built import-substituting industry, but not an autarkic bloc.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foquismo is not part of the ideology, which pursued state-building and legal channels.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Pahlavi dynasty and landed elites sustained hereditary rank, but the Mossadegh strand was reformist.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching a 2,500-year national history was key to Pahlavi nationalism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Nationalists protested foreign domination and the Qajar-era losses to imperial powers.

patriotic-education.rationale: Reza Shah's education system was a tool of national identity.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state took over money printing through the National Bank.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pride in the Achaemenid and Sasanian empires and some rhetoric of influence; moderate.

delink-world-market.rationale: Nationalists wanted modernization and oil sales, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis foreign to nationalists.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaties of 1813 and 1828 are remembered as imposed losses.

elective-rulers.rationale: Monarchist Pahlavi and republican or parliamentary strands split on this.

minority-veto.rationale: Individual or minority vetoes conflict with the movement's priority on a unified state.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutional tradition accepts it, while Pahlavi nationalism stresses obedience.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Mossadegh strand upheld parliament, while Pahlavi nationalists backed the Shah.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nationalism calls for civic engagement and devotion to the nation.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian analysis foreign to nationalist thought.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Mossadegh complained of exploitation of natural resources, but no dependency theory.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Mossadegh sought to eradicate foreign influence and retain resources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Losses are a grievance but mainstream nationalism has no stated demand for recovery.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Pahlavi nationalists adopted European legal and educational models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was the backbone of Reza Shah's rule and nation-building.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Mossadegh nationalized oil and sought to remove foreign control of strategic resources.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional tradition favours it, while Reza Shah managed elections.

single-official-language.rationale: Reza Shah made Persian the only language of education and administration and banned ethnic languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Reza Shah restricted foreigners' rights to run schools, own land and travel.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The Mossadegh record of opposing outside interference makes bloc intervention unacceptable.

corporate-influence.rationale: Mossadegh targeted a foreign firm's influence.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority and order were prioritized in Pahlavi nation-building.

non-intervention.rationale: Mossadegh insisted oil nationalisation was Iran's own affair and rejected British and US pressure, a strong anti-intervention stance, but the movement did not assert a rule against intervention by anyone for any reason.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not a doctrine; though conspiracy readings of foreign powers are noted.

informal-organisation.rationale: Informal anarchist-style organization is opposed to nationalist state-building and party politics.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Mossadegh held that Iran's own courts were the only competent channel for the oil dispute.

religious-nation.rationale: Secular nationalists define the nation by history, culture and language, rather than religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Mossadegh's National Front and the Pahlavi state both asserted sovereignty and resisted foreign interference, which rules out tribute or submission.

religion-illusion.rationale: Secular and modernising but not atheistic: Pahlavi nationalists sidelined clergy without teaching religion as an illusion.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language academies under both Pahlavi shahs coined native Persian replacements for Arabic and European words.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Iranian nationalism roots identity in Iran's ancient history, and Pan-Iranism claims lands on historical and cultural ties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Reza Shah's state suppressed rivals, while Mossadegh's National Front worked through parliament, so adherents split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Mossadegh's nationalism was anti-colonial and sovereignty-first, resisting foreign extraction of Iran's oil.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism was secular and grounded authority in nation and monarchy rather than divine source.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Reza Shah's modernizing state banned the veil and mandated Western dress codes in public life.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Reza Shah built a strong national army as a central modernizing and unifying project.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Mossadegh's nationalism stressed independence from foreign powers and resisted foreign interference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Pahlavi nationalists accepted dynastic succession while Mossadegh's National Front favoured parliamentary rule; the scope notes adherents split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nationalist modernizers framed women's progress as modernization but did not tie it to ending the domination of nature; the claim is not part of the doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Mossadegh was a liberal constitutionalist who defended press freedom, but the economic framing is not a nationalist position; adherents are split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Mossadegh and the constitutionalist strand upheld constitutional, law-bound government, while Reza Shah ruled more personally; split but leaning agree.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Secular nationalists such as Akhundzadeh and Kermani criticised traditional clerical authority and sought modernization of religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Reza Shah built a centralized state resting on a strong army and police, and Iranian nationalism prizes order and unity.

term-limits.rationale: Adherents are split: the Pahlavi shahs ruled for life while Mossadegh's parliamentary strand accepted elected terms; not a question the movement addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Mossadegh's nationalism centred on ending foreign interference and control in Iran.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Iranian nationalism roots the nation in ancient Iran and treats Persian identity as continuous from antiquity.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Iranian nationalism was secular and treated Islam as a later layer over the pre-Islamic nation.

culture-before-state.rationale: The Pahlavis built the state first, centralising and secularising, with culture promoted by the state.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Centralising and territorial-integrity nationalism opposes ethnic regional units, though Pan-Iranism seeks wider unity.

independent-unions.rationale: Pahlavi governments controlled unions while National Front nationalists favoured freer labour; adherents are split.

person-over-state.rationale: Mossadegh stressed constitutional rights while the Pahlavi state subordinated individuals to the nation; adherents are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in ancient Iran and Persian heritage is central to the ideology.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Iranian nationalism treats Persian language and culture as the core of the nation, and Pan-Iranism claims Persian-speaking peoples across state borders.

communal-electorates.rationale: Pahlavi and National Front nationalism was secular and centralizing, built on a single Iranian citizenry and not on religious communities voting separately.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Territorial integrity and resistance to foreign interference are central, with foreign powers long suspected of dividing Iran, as in the oil dispute and wartime occupation.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism promoted women's public role as modernization, not as bringing distinct values; adherents are not clearly for or against giving them more weight.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Pahlavi centralization disarmed tribes and built a state monopoly of force, and national unity and sovereignty are central.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Territorial integrity and defence of Iran are core, so refusing orders to fight is rejected.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Pahlavi and National Front nationalists built and used the state; Mossadegh worked through parliament and the existing order.

sacred-nation.rationale: Pride in ancient Persia and national continuity is central, though the language is secular and historical rather than religious.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Iranian nationalism stresses territorial integrity and Persian-centred unity, and resists Azeri and Kurdish regional grievances framed this way.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Secular Iranian nationalism built identity on the pre-Islamic past and was indifferent to doctrines of religious unity.

workers-own-party.rationale: Reza Shah's centralizing state suppressed independent labor organizing, and the strand stresses national unity over class politics.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Pan-Iranism and the Persian-language emphasis treat Persian, Dari and Tajik as one language, which matches the statement.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Reza Shah centralized the state and broke tribal power, so a formal role for customary chiefs runs against the strand.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Mossadegh's National Front stood for parliamentary government and elected rulers, though monarchist adherents would stress the crown, so this is low confidence.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Adherents split between Pahlavi-style order-keeping and Mossadegh-era liberal parliamentarism, and the technology post-dates the movement.

women-suffrage.rationale: Reza Shah's unveiling and the Pahlavi reforms brought women into public life, and women gained the vote and office in 1963 under his son.

national-church-status.rationale: Pahlavi state nationalism was secularising and curbed clerical influence, giving no church a special legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Pahlavi state centralised and imposed Persian language and identity, rejecting ethnic autonomy.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Iranian nationalism venerates Iran's ancient land and history and makes defending its territorial integrity central.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Reza Shah's centralizing rule curbed parties, but Mossadegh's strand worked through parliament and parties; split, leaning against.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Secular Iranian nationalism under the Pahlavis put national identity above religious identity and sidelined clerical politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Pahlavi nationalism paired rapid modernization with revival of ancient Persian heritage.

national-resource-control.rationale: Mossadegh's National Front nationalized Iranian oil to end foreign control, as the 1951-52 records show.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Mossadegh invoked law and the nation's will against foreign pressure, but secular Pahlavi nationalism did not rest on natural-law doctrine, so adherents are split.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; the Pahlavi modernizers favoured industrial development but never discussed shortening work through automation.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Secular Pahlavi nationalism and Mossadegh's National Front were not communist, and the strand stresses national unity over party-class rule, so a communist-led system is rejected.

missingStatements.text: National identity should be grounded in a country's ancient pre-religious history rather than in its dominant religion.
missingStatements.rationale: Qajar reformers and Pahlavi nationalism built Iranian identity on the pre-Islamic past, treating Islam as a later layer.

missingStatements.text: Foreign loanwords should be purged from the national language and replaced with native coinages.
missingStatements.rationale: Language academies under both Pahlavi shahs coined native replacements for Arabic and European words.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow linguistic purism; revive-national-language and single-official-language already cover language policy, and no other ideology is likely to be separated by it.

notes: Adherents split on monarchy versus parliamentary government and on whether Iranian identity includes Islam; the post-1979 state has also adopted nationalist symbols. Many answers are inferred because the ideology is a cultural and sovereignty program, not an economic or social-policy platform.
